author: davidfelipe96
quote:
13 Years of Waiting for This? Rockstar Has Lost Its Identity.

Score: 0/10

After 13 years of waiting, GTA VI is one of the biggest disappointments I've ever experienced in gaming.

GTA used to stand for freedom, controversy, dark humor, and the ability to do almost anything in an open world. Unfortunately, GTA VI feels like a watered-down, politically correct version of what this franchise once represented.

- Removed adult content: Prostitutes and spontaneous sexual encounters were part of GTA's controversial identity. Their removal makes the game feel unnecessarily sanitized. Even intimate interactions between Jason and Lucia are extremely limited. GTA is an adult-rated game, so why does Rockstar suddenly seem afraid of adult themes?

- Limited player freedom: Too many aspects of the game feel restricted. From relationships to personal choices and activities, Rockstar seems more interested in controlling the player's experience than offering a truly open world.

- Frustrating progression mechanics: Losing money stored in your house and dealing with restrictions on personal belongings makes the experience unnecessarily frustrating.

- A disappointing direction for the franchise: Instead of pushing boundaries like previous GTA titles, GTA VI feels overly cautious and politically correct. The rebellious, provocative spirit that made GTA legendary seems to be disappearing.

Rockstar had 13 years, enormous resources, and an opportunity to create the ultimate open-world experience. Instead, we received a game that feels more restrictive in several important areas than its predecessors.

I wanted a GTA that expanded player freedom, relationships, adult activities, property ownership, and immersion. Not a game that takes away features and limits personal choices.

13 years for this woke garbage? Are you serious, Rockstar?

Bring back the freedom, the controversy, and the real GTA identity.
